FOREWORD This standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Marine Instruments and Safety Aids Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. Gyro-compass are fitted on board while navigating at sea. ship to indicate the ships heading and for taking of bearing

IMO stipulates provision of a Gyro Compass for ships of 500 tons gross tonnage and upwards with the following requirements: a) Master Gyro Compass steering position. or a Gyro Repeater clearly readable by the Helmsman at the Main

b) On ships of 1600 tons gross tonnage and above a Gyro Repeater or Gyro Repeaters shall be provided and shall be suitably placed for taking bearing as nearly as practicable over an arc of the horizon of 360 degrees. This Indian Standard is based on IS0 8728 : 1987 `Shipbuilding - Marine gyro-compasses', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) and IMO Resolution A. 424 (XI) `Performance standards for gyro-copasses'. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4.3 The compass card shall be graduated at equal intervals of 1" (degree of latitude ) or fraction thereof. The graduation error shall be less than kO'2". A numerical indication shall be provided at least at every IO", starting from 000" clockwise through 360". 4.4 Fully adequate illumination shall be provided to enable the reading of ail compass cards at all times. Facilities for dimming shall be provided. 4.5 Both master compass and repeater compasses shall be provided with a lubber line to indicate the ship's heading. 4.5.1 The base or some other fixed extremity of the compass shall be marked or identified in such of the a way as to facilitate the installation compass in a ship so that the lubber line lies in a vertical fore and aft plane of the ship. Where a gyro-compass has the facility of introducing a correction by moving the lubber line, the correction during installation shall be set to zero. 4.5.2 If such marks or identifications are not in the same vertical plane as the uncorrected lubber line, the horizontal angular relationship between them shall be clearly indicated. 4.6 Means shall be provided for correcting the errors induced by speed and latitude. Graphical or tabular means of correction may be used.

5 ACCURACY IN LATITUDE 5.1 Settling Time

UP TO 60"

When switched on in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions the compass shall settle within 6 h. 5.2 Settle Point Error 52.1 The settle point error as defined in 3.10 at any heading shall not exceed 10'75" x secant latitude, and the RMS value of the differences between individual heading indications and the mean value shall be less than 0'25" x secant latitude. 5.2.2 The repeatability of settle point error from one run-up to another shall be within 0'25" x secant latitude. 5.3 Settling Time Under Operational Conditions When switched on in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, the compass shall settle within 6 h when rolling and pitching with simple harmonic motion of any period between 6 and 15 s, a maximum angle of 9, and maximum horizontal acceleration of 0'22 m/sZ. 5.4 Settle Point Error Under General Conditions

The repeatability of the settle point error of the master compass shall be within rt 1" X secant latitude under the general conditions and including variations in magnetic fields likely to be experienced in the ship in which it is installed. 5.5 Residual Error in Correction The residual steady state error, after correction for speed and course influences at a speed of 20 knots, shall not exceed rtO.25" X secant latitude. 5.6 Effect of Alteration of Speed The error due to a rapid alteration 20 knots shall not exceed +2". 3 of speed on

None of the recorded headings shall depart from the original datum by more than 1" x secant latitude. 6.8.2 Frequency Variation Test The supply frequency shall be set to 5 percent above the rlotiinal value for 3 h, during which time thecompass heading shall be recorded at 20 minute intervals. The supply frequency shall then be set to a value 5 percent below nominal for 3 h and the compass heading again recorded at 20 minute intervals. None of the recorded headings shall depart from the original datum by more than 1" x secant latitude. 6.8.3 Vibration Test

When so mounted, the compass shall be settled ( see 3.9 ) and the settle point heading shall be obtained ( see 3.11 ) with the device stationary and nominally level. The device shall then be submitted to the motion previously described having a peak acceleration of. 1'0 f ,O't m/s2 with a periodic time of not less than 3 s,,for.a duration of 2 h. Any difference between the compass heading recorded during the motion and the settle point heading prior to the motion will be considered as due to the motion; it shall not exceed 1" x secant latitude.
6.7.2
NOTE - The compass heading recorded during the motion shall discount any modulation at frequencies equal to or higher than the frequency of the applied motion.

The master compass shall be subjected to the vibration described below. Three separate tests shall be clrried out, the direction of vibration being: a) + 30 f 1" to the meridian and horizontal; b) - 60 & 1" to the meridian and horizontal; and c) vertical. 6.8.3.1.3' In each case the compass shall be settled initially and then the vibration shall be applied at the lowest frequency, holding the appropriate vibration amplitude for a period of 25 minutes as indicated in Table 1. At the end of that period, the frequency and amplitude shall be changed to the next value tabulated below and held for a further 25 minutes. This process shall continue until the entire frequency range has been covered.

6.8 Environmental Test In all the environmental tests, the datum from which settle point variations shall be megsured is the settle point heading obtained in the absence of the particular environmental condition to be applied. Where the gyro-compass intiludee repeater compasses, at least one repeater compass of the gyro-compass shall be energised and aligned with the master compass at all times during the course of environmetal tests. 6.8.6.1 This test only applies to compass equipment which includes a bearing repeater compass intended for use on an open deck and only applies to that bearing repeater compass. The repeater compass shall be subjected to a jet of water delivered from 13 mm ( or larger ) diameter hose and a nozzle connected to a domestic water supply having a static pressure of 240 to 345 kPa for a period of 30 minutes. During this period the equipment shall be sprayed from all possible directions from a distance of 3 m. 6.8.6.2 There shall be no ingress of water. Test

6.8.3.2.3 This whole procedure shall be repeated when the equipment is vibrated in two mutually perpendicular directions in the horizontal plane. There shall be no electrical or mechanical failure during any part of this series of tests. 6.8.3.2.4 The indicated heading shall be recorded at the end of each period and any difference between these recorded headings and the datum settle point heading shall be not more than I" X secant latitude during the test. 6.8.4 Temperature Test

6.9.1 This test only applies to compsss equipment which includes a repeater compass. The master compass shall be settled on a level rotary table and the repeater aligned with the master compass The table and master compass shall then be turtled at a rate not greater than 5*/s, the table being stopped at every 30" and the compass heading and the repeater heading recorded. This procedure shall be repeated in the reverse direction of rotation, 6.9.2 The difference between the master compass heading and the repeated compass heading at any point shall be less tnan 0'5". NOTE - The exact angle of the table when readings are taken is unimportant since the object of the test is to compare master and repeater heading indications. 6.9.3 If the repeater compass to be tested is intended for use on an open deck, it shall be tested at a temperature of - 20 * 3�C and again at -I- 60 f 3�C having been exposed to the test temperature for 2 h prior to the test. Any climatically controlled system designed as a part of the repeater installation may be switched on for this test. 6.10 Speed Correction Test 6.10.1 This test applies to compass units fitted with a correction device for speed and course error. 6.10.2 With the master compass mounted on a level and stationary base and the lubber Line of the compass aligned North-South, the master compass shall be settled and the settle point heading recorded. 5

The compass equipment shall be placed in a chamber at normal room temperature, switched on and allowed to settle. The settle point heading [shall be obtained and recorded. The temperature of the chamber shall then be raised to 45 f 2�C and maintained for a period of 3 h. At the end of this period, the compass heading indication shall again be recorded. The temperature of the chamber shall then be reduced to 0 rt- 2�C and maintained at this temperature for 3 h.%`At the end of this period the compass heading indication shall be recorded once more. Neither of the recorded heading indications shall differ from the: datum settle point heading by more than 1" x secant latitude. NOTE -When-the temperature of the chamber is being changed it shall not alter by a rate which exceeds 45�C per hour. 6.8.5 Damp Heat Test

6.8.5.1 The compass equipment shall be placed in a chamber at normal room temperature and humidity, switched on and allowed to settle. The

8.1 Information shall be provided to enable competent members of a ship's crew to operate and maintain the equipment efficiently. 9 ADVICE TO SHIP SURVEYORS FOR THE INSTALLATION OF GYRO-CONIPASSES AND REPEATER COMPASSES ON BOARD SHIPS 9.1 To ensure that the errors induced by the motions specified in 6.8 are not exceeded in practice, it will be necessary to pay particular attention to the siting of the master compass. 9.2 Where the master compass and/or any repeated compasses are to be used for taking bearings, then the horizontal angle between the vertical plane passing through the centre of the compass card, including the lubber line and the vertical plane passing through the ship's fore and aft datum line, shall be within IfrO.5" when installed.

The sound level generated by units of the gyrocompass which is installed on the navigation deck shall be measured with a sound level indicator by placing it 1 m away from the surface of the sound generating part. The measured sound level shall be 65 dB or less. However, no measurement shall be made at the time of starting the gyro-compass. 7 MARKING AND PACKING shall be
